samples.identification: NET Reactor protected managed remote-control and collection implant
samples.marker_line: Protected CLR implant: concealed commands and capture uploads
judgment_evidence: Native main at 0x4019f0 extracts RT_RCDATA/__ and uses a two-pass neighboring-byte substitution decoder, independently reproduced from its pure table initializer at 0x401300. The checksum-valid size-prefixed zlib output contains a CLR version prefix and a managed PE.

Managed bootstrap carries its real entry image in resource _. The LDFgNmI4H method decrypts a 65,892-byte patch stream; bounded data-only interpretation recovered it before stopping at unsupported Assembly.GetModules. Applying 2,610 records restores method headers.

b3nMWnkTO decodes 1,650 field-to-method mappings. Resolving 10,898 delegate-proxy calls exposes task dispatch and concealed process/script execution, targeted clipboard collection and desktop capture, archive construction and HTTP upload.

Entry method 680 (74V.PEs.627) reaches task runner 833 (ab2.2J2.nC6). Capture helpers feed archive member insertion through kJk.J3H/C75.Xt4; archive bytes and direct screenshots reach HtQ.wN8/E2P (711/712), E65.F4j (815) and E65.48o (816), whose request stream writes the encoded multipart bytes and obtains the response.

Concealed remote tasking and surveillance-to-upload behavior tip the verdict. Commercial protection and ordinary HTTP/process APIs alone do not. The submitted multi-family name and vendor labels are not used as family proof.
missing_context: Exact family and still-virtualized configuration/C2 strings are unresolved. No host authorization, intended operator, or live connectivity established. No sample entry point or OS/network effect was executed.

uncovered_hostile_behaviors: received task to hidden command/script execution
clipboard collection to archive and outbound upload
work_attempted: Original atomscan, cleave facts including available decoded strings, cleave strings, and Rizin control-flow inspection
Native resource decoding and managed resource extraction
Bounded method-patch recovery, delegate call restoration, ILSpy decompilation, and scans/facts on recovered assemblies
Reviewed original evidence for structural fingerprints, API names, decoder, runtime-hosting and resource extraction; retained accurate suspicious protection rule
coverage_gap.limitation: Original scans expose only native wrapper bytes. YAML cannot execute its custom resource decoder, restore encrypted CIL method headers or resolve delegate proxies. Recovered assemblies expose neutral APIs but current matchable facts do not bind hostile sources to sinks. Neither packing nor API co-occurrence justifies new hostile detections. Automated decoding and managed data-flow support are required.

samples.identification: Rifaien native VM self-submission test client, UPX packed, with incomplete appended PE
samples.marker_line: Rifaien VM client: self-submission; detect incomplete appended PE
judgment_evidence: Reproduced NRV2B decompression, independently recomputed the compressed and expanded Adler32 values, repaired checksums only on an analysis copy, and obtained official UPX decompression success. The original was not modified.

The UPX entry stub decompresses and transfers to 0x401130. Main at 0x4013a0 reads GetModuleFileNameA into fopen(rb), seeks/reads its entire own image, locates [[UNIQUE]], and mutates the following 16 bytes.

A loop sleeps 30 seconds, selects NODE1 through NODE7 and a random executable filename, writes the modified self-buffer, and sends it through curl_formadd(file[], node, submit), CURLOPT_URL and CURLOPT_HTTPPOST to the fixed /upload service. It then unlinks that temporary filename and repeats. The server response is not used to fetch or dispatch commands.

The endpoint and node selection fit the documented historical public VM playground. The supplied binary performs self-submission, not arbitrary host-file theft; no persistence, privilege escalation, victim-file infection, downloaded payload activation or received-command execution was established. The mutation and upload detections remain accurate and are preserved.

The 111,616-byte overlay starts at 0x14c00 with 139 NOPs, followed at 0x14c8b by 111,477 bytes of an incomplete PE. All but two bytes of this prefix equal the second submitted native wrapper. Its declared remaining sections, imports and protected resources extend beyond EOF. No loader reference/activation path was found in the self-submission program. This is incomplete inert data, not a runnable second stage.
missing_context: Current endpoint ownership and liveness could not be verified: forager HTTP did not complete in over six minutes; bounded HTTPS retry failed with TLS handshake timeouts. No dependencies are referenced beyond statically linked libcurl and OS/CRT libraries.
The operator and original deployment authorization are unknown. BENIGN judges the test client purpose and traced code; it does not assert an authorized deployment on every machine.
samples.external_label_explanation: Self-replication, uniqueness mutation causing invalid UPX checksums, outbound executable submissions, and an appended prefix of a protected implant explain generic malware and sandbox labels. An inert malware prefix and a research submission destination do not establish local execution of that implant or a C2 command handler.

trait_change.claim: An appended standard PE header has a complete bounded section table but a nonempty section raw extent exceeds container EOF.
trait_change.placement: metadata/binary/layout/embedded: relationship between an embedded executable layout and container extent, not execution or malware identity.
trait_change.generalization: No sample names, addresses, hashes, exact sizes, campaign endpoints or family labels required. Accepts PE32 and PE32+ and iterates bounded section tables.
trait_change.controls: Eight inert PE controls in testdata/taxonomy/embedded-overlay-bounds. Truncated PE32 and PE32+ match; complete images, malformed signature, short header, mapped header and absent overlay do not. All eight passed.
trait_change.consumers: Exact and ancestor selectors inspected. No references modified. Broad metadata/binary downgrade and metadata/binary/layout exclusion already had matching original evidence. Final scans expose no newly triggered hostile or suspicious consumers.
trait_change.preservation: No matcher removal, narrowing or severity reduction. All prior original and recovered-stage findings retained.

classifier_disagreement: Both implants still render scan benign despite malicious recovered behavior. Model v18.18 feature schema v18 warns that the engine expects v21. Rifaien renders benign, agreeing with manual judgment. Probability/confidence is not treated as a malicious verdict.
archives: All submitted artifacts are PE files, not archives. Protected resources are not automatically exposed as analyzable members. Independently recovered stages were separately scanned before and after; stage deltas are recorded below.

research_sources.role: Historical contemporaneous public VM discussion; corroboration only.
Historical description of seven public-upload VMs; secondary context, not behavior proof.
